transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I suppose I'm here because of my evenings. I've been having these nights where I just... eat. And then I end up just sitting there with all these crumbs and empty containers around me. 

It's... I don't really like talking about it. I just feel so ashamed and disgusted with myself afterwards. It's gotten to the point where I can hardly even pray... or look folks at church in the eye the next morning.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating during these nights?

No... I don't. It's like... well, once the house is quiet and I take that first bite, my good sense just steps aside. I'll be sitting there, telling myself, 'Belinda, stop now,' but... my hands just keep reaching for more. I can't seem to make it stop.
Do you feel guilty after these eating episodes?
Yes... like I was saying before. It's just an awful feeling. I sit there looking at the mess, all the empty containers and crumbs, and... I just feel so ashamed. Disgusted, really.
Do you ever try to make up for these eating episodes by purging, exercising, or doing anything else to counteract the calories you consumed?
No... I don't do anything like that. I just... go to bed.
How often do these nights of eating like this happen?
...Well. Ever since my friend passed away, it's been... I suppose at least once or twice most weeks. There really hasn't been a month where it just... let up.
During these nights, do you typically eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, like within a couple of hours?

...Yes. I suppose so. On a bad night, I'll... I'll start with a plate of leftover funeral-luncheon casserole. And before I know it, I've eaten that, and... half a pan of brownies. Some biscuits. Whatever chicken salad is in the fridge. Just... all in one sitting.
Have you noticed a decrease in interest in activities or hobbies that you used to enjoy since your friend passed away?
...No. I don't think so. I still... do my usual things. I haven't really noticed a change with that.
Do you think these nights of eating happen when you're feeling particularly upset or stressed about something, like your friend's passing?
...I don't know. Maybe. I try not to think about it too much. It just... happens, I guess.
Do you think these nights of eating happen when you are feeling sad or upset about your friend's passing?
...I think you just asked me that. But... like I said, I don't really know. I just... I just eat. I don't really sit there and analyze why I'm doing it.
Do you think eating like this makes you feel better, even if it's just for a little while?
...I'm not sure. I guess... maybe while I'm doing it. But mostly I just... I just feel worse after.
Do you think eating like this is a way for you to deal with difficult emotions?
...I don't know. It's just... eating. I'm not really trying to deal with anything, I don't think. It just happens.
Do you usually feel upset or emotional right before one of these eating episodes starts?
...I don't really pay attention to that. I just... I don't know. I'm not really tracking how I feel before it starts.
Do you think these eating episodes would happen if you weren't feeling upset or emotional about something?
...I really couldn't say. Like I said, I don't think about it like that. I don't know if being upset has anything to do with it... I couldn't tell you if it would happen anyway or not.
Do you think these eating episodes are triggered by feeling sad or upset about your friend's passing or anything else?

...I'd really rather not talk about my friend. I just... I don't think it's connected like that. I'm not sitting there crying and then going to the kitchen, it's just... I don't know why it happens. I just eat.
Do you think the eating happens because you're trying to comfort yourself or escape from feeling upset?

I don't... I don't really look at it like that. I'm not sitting there thinking about comforting myself or... escaping. I just... I don't know what I'm trying to do. I don't really have an answer for you.
Do you think the eating happens as a reaction to feeling upset or sad?
I... I feel like you just asked me that. Like I said, I really don't know. I don't think it's a reaction to anything. It just... happens. I don't know how else to answer that for you.
Do you think these eating episodes would stop if your emotional distress about your friend's passing and other issues were resolved?

I... look, I asked you please not to bring her up. I don't know. I don't know what would happen. If I knew how to make it stop, I wouldn't be sitting here. I just... I really don't have an answer to that.
Do you think your eating episodes are related to feeling upset or emotional?

I... I really don't know what else to say about this. You keep asking me the same thing in different ways, and... I just don't know. I'm not making a connection like that in my head. It's just... I just eat. That's all I can tell you.
Do you think your eating episodes would happen if you were not feeling any emotional distress?
I... we just keep going in circles with this. I've told you, I really don't know. I can't tell you what would happen if things were different. I just... I don't have an answer for you.
Do you think your eating episodes would stop if you were feeling happy and calm?
I... look, I'm sorry, but I really can't answer that. I don't know what it would take to make it stop. I'm just... I'm not sure.
